title.analysis: Authentic title "The 3 'Silent' Fees Destroying Your Wealth (Not Taxes)" is a hidden-cost list with a negation hook. The script names three costs (investment fees, inflation and cash drag, the behaviour gap); only the first is a literal fee, and the third is presented twice. The promise is delivered, with metaphorical "fees".

script.stored_text_completeness: All 21354 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored ending is complete ("It stayed with you."); the behaviour-gap section and the action plan each appear twice with different numbers (timing loss 3% then 4%; incomes $200,000/$60,000 then $300,000/$70,000), and the second gap section is introduced as "the third silent fee" again, which points to concatenated generated drafts; ASR garbles ("Co" for COVID, "bare markets", "1.4 4%"); audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: You know what's fascinating about human behavior? We'll spend 20 minutes arguing with a barista over being charged for oat milk, but we'll watch half a million dollars evaporate from our retirement account and just shrug. I watched my neighbor nearly have a breakdown last week because his gym raised their monthly fee by $3. $3. This same guy lost 42,000 in his 401k last year to fees he didn't even know existed. And when I mentioned it, he looked
script.ending_words: You can't control the market. You can't control inflation, but you can control whether you volunteer to lose. Stop paying fees you don't have to pay. Stop letting cash melt. Stop trying to be clever when boring wins. The money you save won't feel dramatic today, but 30 years from now, when everyone else is wondering where it all went, you'll know exactly where yours went. It stayed with you.
script.analysis: Full 21354 canonical characters read. A single-narrator hidden-costs explainer: hook (gym fee vs 401(k) fees), fee 1 (expense ratios, $10,000/year comparison, Bogle), fee 2 (inflation and cash drag), fee 3 (behaviour gap: DALBAR, March 2020 panic sale, loss aversion, automation), a 40-year two-versions simulation, a late-starter section, an action plan, then a second behaviour-gap section (best days, 2021 dip-waiting, Buffett), a second action plan and a close. Core arithmetic reproduces; savings-rate, COVID-recovery and $200,000 late-starter figures are overstated, and the duplicated sections with conflicting numbers suggest concatenated drafts.
beat_map: Hook: oat milk and gym fees vs invisible fees.
Where to find expense ratios; index funds.
Fee 2: inflation and cash drag; HYSA.
Fee 3: behaviour gap; DALBAR; March 2020 panic sale.
Behaviour gap again: best days, 2021 dip-waiting, Buffett.
